races.name: West 'Howya' Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Whats New
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with consistent placed form at 2m+ on Good going, four placings from nine similar-going runs, and jockey Cian Quirke knows the horse having ridden it recently; races close to the pace and is well-suited to tracking a single front-runner.|

runners_data.name: Alfinthesea
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with no recent form to assess, style unknown, and the going tag is flagged uncertain — Kieren Buckley takes the ride for a trainer running at modest strike rate, making this largely a speculative entry requiring a big step forward.|

runners_data.name: Breezingwithdstars
runners_data.note: JJ Slevin booked for a hold-up horse that has a worrying tendency to fade in finishes; four runs on Good-equivalent going all ended outside the places, and that consistent fading pattern is a serious concern over this stamina-testing trip.|

runners_data.name: First Ascent
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy's presence for Gordon Elliott (9/48 in 14 days) is the headline angle — a hold-up horse with three placings from seven similar-going runs who was placed at 2m4f+ before stepping back in trip; 70 days off adds a fitness question but the yard runs horses fit.|

runners_data.name: Kilmond Knight
runners_data.note: Very lightly raced with just one run on record at a longer trip on Good ground, producing an unknown finishing position; the claim jockey and a trainer with zero runners in the past 14 days offer little confidence, and a pulled-up run last time increases the concern.|

runners_data.name: Minnatrix
runners_data.note: Prominent type who placed at 2m on Good going but has also fallen and been pulled up; the headgear hood was tried previously, and the pattern of form — a second followed by erratic outings — suggests inconsistency that makes this hard to trust.|

runners_data.name: No Mon No Fun
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with one run at 2m4f on Good ground finishing fourth; the tongue-tie is noted, and with a 19-day turnaround and a trainer with no recent runners, there is insufficient evidence to rate the chance reliably in either direction.|

runners_data.name: Rumi Rock
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a clear fading-in-finish flag and only one comparable run — a tenth at 2m4f on Good — to work from; Phillip Enright rides but the profile of finishing weak and racing from off a steady pace does not inspire confidence in a scenario where the front-runner controls tempo.|

runners_data.name: Sharu
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's runner carries the yard's know-how and Darragh O'Keeffe is a quality booking; placed twice from four similar-ground runs and races prominently, meaning this horse is ideally placed to track World As One and challenge from two out.|

runners_data.name: World As One
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner for Mullins and O'Keeffe, has placed at 2m4f on Soft and shown consistency across three similar-going runs; the tongue-tie is retained and the uncontested lead at Ballinrobe's turning track on Good ground makes this the pivotal horse in any race-shape reading.|

runners_data.name: Lady Felicia
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with one run at 2m on Good finishing fourth; Simon Torrens takes the ride for Aidan Howard, but the tongue-tie first time, a 56-day absence, and total lack of form depth make this an almost pure unknown in a competitive Maiden field.|

runners_data.name: Middlethird Marvel
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse tagged as fading in finishes, five runs on Good-equivalent ground and not once placed; the claim jockey Conor Smithers (7lb) and a hood plus tongue-tie in headgear suggests the trainer is experimenting rather than expecting a breakthrough.|

runners_data.name: Phyllis Rodda
runners_data.note: 275 days off the track is an enormous concern regardless of anything else; Mark Walsh's booking is the one compelling detail for Barry Connell's runner, but two pulled-up runs and going unknown mean this is a major fitness and form risk off a long layoff.|

races.paceDynamic: World As One is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no rival willing to push for the lead, Sean O'Keeffe can dictate an entirely uncontested gallop from the front under Willie Mullins' direction. The prominent types — Whats New, Minnatrix, and Sharu — will likely settle into a tracking position just off the pace, meaning World As One faces zero early pressure and can control the tempo to suit. On Good ground at Ballinrobe, a single front-runner setting a measured, sustainable pace over 2m1½f creates a race that will be run at an even rhythm with the decisive moment coming at the last flight, not in a prolonged grind. This shape strongly favours hold-up horses with a clean late run, provided they get a clear passage, but also rewards any prominent tracker who travels comfortably throughout and finds extra when asked — horses like First Ascent and Sharu profile best to benefit from this controlled shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: World As One Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If World As One is permitted to dictate a measured, unchallenged pace and quickens off the final hurdle
scenarios.body: World As One settles into a rhythm no rival will disturb, conserving enough energy through the final turn to repel challenges at the death on Good ground; the Mullins/O'Keeffe combination is well-placed to exploit a straightforward lead scenario in a Maiden Hurdle with a weak front-running market

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If World As One's lead is sustainable but a prominent tracker travels easily throughout and picks up sharply from two out
scenarios.body: Whats New has repeatedly placed at this trip on Good ground and Sharu showed a placed effort at 2m in similar conditions, both sitting close enough to strike before the tiring leader; the De Bromhead/O'Keeffe partnership behind Sharu adds professional weight to a horse who races close to pace and hits form on this surface

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just quick enough to spread the field and a staying hold-up type delivers a sustained late run from the back
scenarios.body: First Ascent, handled by Jack Kennedy for Gordon Elliott, has placed three times from the back-half of the field on similar ground and at comparable distances, suggesting a genuine staying profile that could benefit if the race develops any galloping tempo; the caution is that with one soft front-runner the pace may not be strong enough to fully set up a late finisher

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Upsets Market
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent horses crowd the early pace or World As One makes a jumping error, fracturing the race shape
scenarios.body: A messy early race at a small field Irish Maiden Hurdle could open the door for a lightly-raced type like Alfinthesea or Phyllis Rodda to outrun their profile under market-connected pilots; the probability is low given World As One's clear mandate, but the presence of several unknowns in an unpredictable Maiden adds a small tail risk

watchPoints.text: World As One — if Sean O'Keeffe allows the field to creep up on his heels approaching the turn for home, the single-pace front-runner may find rivals passing without a fight; watch for how much daylight he holds at the top of the straight.

First Ascent — Jack Kennedy will want a clear run from off the pace, but in a 13-runner Maiden over a tight circuit, traffic at the final two hurdles could cost him momentum and the race; watch his position rounding the final bend.

Breezingwithdstars — JJ Slevin's profile as a top-tier jockey may tempt punters, but this horse's consistent fading pattern in four runs on similar going is a structural concern; watch whether it capitulates again from two out.

Phyllis Rodda — a 275-day layoff combined with two previous pulled-up runs and unknown going preference means Mark Walsh could be riding a racecourse workout; worth monitoring in-running to see if it is sent to the front as a surprise pacemaker.

Sharu — De Bromhead horses can arrive fit off a 36-day break and this horse's prominent style gives O'Keeffe every chance to shadow World As One throughout; watch how close Darragh O'Keeffe elects to race to the leader from the outset as a guide to stable confidence.

races.name: David Heneghan Memorial Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Bhean Saibhre
runners_data.note: Lone front-runner in the race with solid Good-ground form (1W3P in similar conditions) and 19 days fresh; holds a STYLE_FIT flag suggesting she is technically operating out of her most natural role, but as the only horse willing to lead she owns the pace and that lends her a structural advantage, not a handicap.
runners_data.comment: A winner four starts back, and fourth three starts back, she's fresh again just 19 days on and already has today's trip and going covered. Second on our figures, her rounded profile makes her the pick here, an eighth last time out the only blemish.

runners_data.name: Houndsworth
runners_data.note: Four-year-old hold-up type with one win and a placed effort from 11 Good-ground runs; trainer McNiff in form at 3/11 over 14 days and Phillip Enright takes the ride, which is a positive booking — needs the pace to be sustainable rather than pedestrian given his closing style over this trip.
runners_data.comment: A winner three starts back is the standout form in this book, with a seventh and a sixth in the two starts since. He has today's trip and going covered, and a 37-day break plus third spot on our figures make him the leading danger here.

runners_data.name: Le Diablo
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with strong Good-ground credentials (11 runs, 1W2P, all on Good) and trainer Ryan in sharp form at 5/25; J J Slevin is an excellent booking and Le Diablo's natural position just off the pace suits this scenario perfectly if Bhean Saibhre controls the front — most naturally suited to the dominant race shape.
runners_data.comment: A second last time out catches the eye, with a win five starts back among the form but little of note in between. He's quick to return here 18 days on with today's trip and going covered, sitting mid-table on our figures just below his official mark.

runners_data.name: Doctor Confusion
runners_data.note: Unknown style with a 349-day absence from the track — that layoff is the primary concern before any tactical discussion; trained by De Bromhead and ridden by Darragh O'Keeffe, the yard has the firepower to return a horse fit first-time up, but the form string of 68/6P- on just three comparable runs offers limited confidence.
runners_data.comment: A pulled-up effort last time out caps a book that also shows two sixths and an eighth, and he returns here from a 349-day absence. He does have today's trip and going covered, but our figures rate him well below his official mark, making him hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Valsorpresa
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up type with an enormous sample on Good ground (15 runs, 1W3P) giving high confidence he handles conditions; Harry Sexton (7) claims 7lbs which aids the handicap mark, but Valsorpresa's tendency to finish mid-pack in his recent starts — six 16f runs, all single-figure finishes — suggests a horse that competes without threatening.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts with nothing better than a fifth, the recent efforts don't inspire confidence on their own. But he has today's trip and going covered, and our figures rate him top of this field and well clear of his official mark, making him the leading danger on figures alone.

runners_data.name: Marlpark
runners_data.note: John Patrick Ryan's second string here; in truth a genuine hold-up horse whose best form comes when delivered late (2nd over 19f on Soft, 4th over 20f Soft), but the redistribution note reflects that too many closers crowd the rear — Daniel King rides and Marlpark needs clean passage from off the pace to be competitive.
runners_data.comment: A second five starts back, and a fourth two starts back, hint at ability, though a pulled-up effort last time out is the obvious blot. He has today's trip and going covered, and off a 46-day break our figures still rate him well above his official mark.

runners_data.name: Max Meridius
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse that fades in the finish — a significant structural concern in a 2m1½f hurdle; Danny Mullins is a high-class booking but Max Meridius's form shows repeated late-race attrition (12th, 9th over 16f) and his trainer has gone 0/4 over the last 14 days, making him hard to back with conviction.
runners_data.comment: A fifth last time out arrests a run that also features a ninth and three unplaced efforts, and he remains winless in his last five. Quick back into action just 12 days on, with today's trip and going covered, our figures nudge him a touch above his official mark.

runners_data.name: Ballinvasas Best
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up type with consistent placing form (two 4ths, one 6th from four recent outings on Good) who fills a space in the field rather than threatening to win it; Sean O'Keeffe rides and the horse handles Good ground reliably, but at OR 82 without a win on his record in this sample he is more likely to be placed than to score.
runners_data.comment: Unplaced last time out and with only a sixth and two fourths further back to hang her form on, she's winless in her last four starts. She does have today's going covered, but bottom spot on our figures off a 52-day break makes her hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: At The Wings
runners_data.note: Six-year-old who has failed to finish better than seventh in his last five starts, all on Good or Heavy ground — the form string of 0000-7 makes grim reading regardless of conditions; Michael Kenneally (5) claims 5lbs but At The Wings' inability to convert despite good ground suitability (9 from 11 runs on Good) suggests a horse limited by ability rather than circumstance.
runners_data.comment: A seventh last time out is the highlight of a book otherwise blank across four unplaced efforts, and he's winless in his last five. Quick to return just nine days on, with today's trip and going covered, our figures rate him well above his modest official mark.

races.paceDynamic: Bhean Saibhre is the lone confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner handicap hurdle over 2m1½f on Good ground at Ballinrobe, and with no genuine challenger likely to press her from the outset, she should be able to dictate a controlled, even gallop throughout. Le Diablo is the only other natural prominent type with a realistic chance of tracking close to the pace, but the bulk of the field — Houndsworth, Valsorpresa, Max Meridius, Marlpark, Ballinvasas Best, and At The Wings — are hold-up horses, several of whom have been redistributed to midfield on the map simply because the rear is overcrowded with closers. Marlpark, Ballinvasas Best, and At The Wings are all true hold-up types who are unlikely to secure their natural late position in a field this heavily loaded with closers, meaning genuine finishing room at the back of the field will be contested and their intended race shapes may not materialise cleanly. A sustainable, uncontested lead set by Bhean Saibhre on Good ground over this trip most strongly favours a well-positioned prominent racer who can travel smoothly in second or third before asserting after the final hurdle, rather than a pure closer who must weave through a cluttered finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bhean Saibhre Leads, Prominent Tracker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Bhean Saibhre sets an uncontested, honest pace and a horse travelling prominently in her wake kicks clear after the last.
scenarios.body: Bhean Saibhre dictates from the front without any serious pressure, keeping the gallop even enough to expose closers but fast enough to stretch them approaching the final flight; a horse locked in second or third throughout needs only to assert their class once the front-runner is collared or fades.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Land Late Off Steady Pace
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely sedate early, the field compresses and a hold-up horse threads through in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: A slow tempo through the first mile bunches the field and allows horses from the middle of the pack to travel without expending energy, setting up a sprint finish to the line; this suits the more athletic hold-up types who can quicken sharply but is complicated by the overcrowded rear of the field where Marlpark, Ballinvasas Best, and At The Wings must all find clear passage.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Wires Field
scenarios.trigger: If Bhean Saibhre stretches the field with a more forceful early gallop and the hold-up horses are left with too much to do from the final turn.
scenarios.body: With no horse willing or able to go with her, Bhean Saibhre dictates every yard of the race and her rivals are strung out before the straight; the hold-up types never get into a rhythm to close and Bhean Saibhre's Good-ground form and front-running resolution carry her to the line.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos In Cluttered Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final half-mile, the hold-up group converges simultaneously and a surprise winner emerges from the pack.
scenarios.body: Multiple hold-up horses attempting to find their natural position in a congested closing section creates interference risks and a messy finish; in this scenario a lightly-weighted horse who has tracked mid-division cleanly benefits more than a confirmed deep closer.

watchPoints.text: Bhean Saibhre sets the pace entirely unchallenged — if she is allowed to dictate a moderate tempo through the first mile, the race could be over as a contest well before the final flight, disadvantaging every hold-up horse in the field.

Le Diablo is the one prominent horse capable of sitting second and launching a serious challenge; if J J Slevin allows him to track Bhean Saibhre without burning petrol, he is the most structurally-placed horse in the field to capitalise on the dominant scenario.

The three redistributed hold-up horses — Marlpark, Ballinvasas Best, and At The Wings — are all likely to be racing in the same section of the track in the closing stages; interference or traffic problems in the final two hurdles are a realistic risk given how many closers are competing for the same ground.

Doctor Confusion's 349-day absence is the single biggest unknown in the race — De Bromhead and Darragh O'Keeffe is a powerful combination that can fire a horse fresh, but without a recent racecourse performance to calibrate fitness, he is a variable that could upset or underperform the pace map entirely.

Max Meridius's fade flag combined with Danny Mullins' elite riding ability creates a watch point — Mullins may attempt to position him more prominently than his natural style to counteract the late-race attrition, which could briefly disrupt the early order if he creeps into a position ahead of where he belongs.

races.name: RBC Brewin Dolphin Rated Novice Hurdle

runners_data.name: Lureka Du Noyer
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter here, her recent winning form over 16f on Good at Ballinrobe translates well to this trip; De Bromhead sends her back quickly after 54 days off, and Darragh O'Keeffe knows the horse — the style-fit flag notes she is technically racing out of full role but as the lone leader she is ideally positioned to exploit this shape.

runners_data.name: Ardeen Joy
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's runner won last time out on Good ground over 20f but her natural prominent style has been displaced to a midfield mapping because the field is simply too full of front-runners; Sam Ewing will need to press forward from the gate to recover her preferred berth, which may cost energy early and compromise her finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Manoir De Mirande
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes the ride for Elliott (9 winners from 48 runners in 14 days) on a four-year-old who won last time over 18f on Good — the combination of in-form trainer, top jockey, and a horse that handles this ground and trip makes this one the most straightforward prominent horse in the field; he ran just nine days ago so freshness is not a concern.

runners_data.name: Crystabel
runners_data.note: Her most recent win also came on Good ground over 18f, giving genuine form claims on paper, but she has been displaced from her natural front-running position by the density of pace in this field; Daniel King will need to find a way to get her into a comfortable rhythm from a compromised starting point, and the style-fit discount applies — her chance is reduced if she cannot get close to the front.

runners_data.name: Eyeeye
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse carrying a fade warning, Eyeeye's best recent effort was a second over 18f on Good but her sim-going record of 12 wins/15 runs in the place column is thin for this level; Jack Gilligan (5lb claim) rides and trainer Paul John Gilligan has not fired in the last 14 days (0/10), making this a difficult win profile even if the pace scenario broke favourably.

runners_data.name: Move It On Over
runners_data.note: J J Slevin is a high-quality jockey on a horse with very limited ability — OR 74 and a 0W0P sim-going record tells the full story; the fade warning and a form string showing an unseated rider and several unplaced efforts suggests this runner needs everything to go right and the principals to go wrong.

races.paceDynamic: Lureka Du Noyer is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival to push her through the early stages, she should settle into a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front on Good ground at Ballinrobe. Manoir De Bromhead and other prominent horses will track closely, but the pace will be set by Lureka Du Noyer alone at a tempo she can dictate rather than one forced upon her. This shape — a single uncontested leader controlling the race from the front — will run to the wire in an orderly fashion with the winner almost certainly coming from those who were close to the pace throughout. This race shape strongly favours races-close-to-the-pace profiles; Lureka Du Noyer and Manoir De Mirande are best placed to capitalise. Critically, this field contains more prominent types than can all secure their natural position — Ardeen Joy and Crystabel are genuine front-to-midfield horses who will likely be shuffled back from where they want to be, compromising their chances.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lureka Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Lureka Du Noyer leads uncontested and settles into a rhythm she dictates throughout.
scenarios.body: Lureka Du Noyer sets a sustainable pace on Good ground and, never put under pressure early, travels well into the straight and kicks clear from the final hurdle; her most recent win came over a similar trip on Good going and this scenario plays directly to that profile. Manoir De Mirande, tracking closely from a prominent position, is the most likely challenger but would need Lureka to stop — horses that stay close throughout prosper most when the leader controls tempo like this.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Gets Up
scenarios.trigger: If Lureka Du Noyer sets a fair gallop but a close-tracking rival picks her off at the last.
scenarios.body: Manoir De Mirande, freshest of the field on just 9 days since his last run and handled well by Jack Kennedy, tracks the leader throughout and produces enough to wear down Lureka Du Noyer in the closing stages; his recent Good-ground win and strong trainer form from Gordon Elliott (9/48 last 14 days) make him the likeliest beneficiary of this shape. Ardeen Joy, if she can recover her natural prominent berth after redistribution, could also feature if the leader weakens.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Messy Pace, Closer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution chaos causes crowding and checking early, and the pace collapses, allowing a hold-up horse to stay on past tired rivals.
scenarios.body: A muddled early order — with Ardeen Joy and Crystabel both trying to push forward from redistributed positions — could disrupt rhythm and produce a pace collapse; in that scenario a fresher-legged hold-up type could stay on into prize money. Eyeeye's second-placed run on Good ground is the best hold-up form available, though the fade warning and weak sim-going record temper expectations significantly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Culls Field Late
scenarios.trigger: If Good ground rides firmer than expected and errors at hurdles cause casualties, leaving a lone survivor to plod home.
scenarios.body: Move It On Over and Eyeeye both carry fade warnings and modest form figures, making them unlikely winners under normal conditions; only a race of significant attrition — fallers, errors, weakeners — could bring them into contention. Move It On Over's OR of 74 and 0W0P sim-going record mean this scenario needs everything to go wrong for the principals.

watchPoints.text: Lureka Du Noyer — if she is allowed to stride clear uncontested at a controlled pace, she becomes very hard to pass; watch whether any rival challenges her for the lead in the first half mile.

Ardeen Joy and Crystabel — both natural prominent types crammed into a midfield mapping; watch for crowding and jostling as they attempt to push forward from their compromised positions in the early stages.

Manoir De Mirande — Jack Kennedy's positioning in the first two flights will be telling; if he slots directly behind Lureka Du Noyer and tracks smoothly, this horse becomes the one most likely to produce a challenge in Scenario B.

Eyeeye — watch the hold-up horses at the top of the hill; if Lureka Du Noyer has already stretched clear and the chasing pack is under pressure, the fade warning on Eyeeye could become very relevant in the closing stages.

Going underfoot — all eight races today at Ballinrobe are on Good; track whether times are coming back faster or slower than expected, as any firming could accelerate the pace collapse that would favour Scenario C or D.

races.name: BOYLE Sports Home Of The Early Payout Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Wolf Prince
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old in career-best form with back-to-back wins on Good, most recently over 18f 9 days ago; hold-up style suits the likely single-pace tempo, and trainer Aidan Melia has a live T14 runner in the book — headgear unchanged, handles this going well.
runners_data.comment: Three wins from his last five starts, the latest three in succession, and he's back within nine days full of running. He has already run over today's trip and going, and tops our figures, making him hard to beat.

runners_data.name: Fiveonefive
runners_data.note: Mark Walsh's booking elevates this hold-up type significantly; has not won recently and moderate sim-going record (0W0P) tempers enthusiasm, but the 23-day break and better ground than last two runs give him a fair platform.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, though a fourth last time hints he's not far away, and he already has today's trip and going under his belt. Second on our figures after 23 days off, the risk is whether that indifferent form turns around here.

runners_data.name: Sir Allen
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner whose ability to control tempo is the pivot of the whole race; tagged STYLE_FIT 0.93 as a nominal Prominent runner, he must sustain for 2m1½f on Good — one previous Good-ground win from 15 runs suggests the surface is not his ally, and the 43-day absence is worth noting.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, though a third three starts back shows he can find a frame, and he already has today's trip and going under his belt. Third on our figures, but a 43-day absence since his last run is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Spinola Bay
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes the ride for Gordon Elliott on a six-year-old who has won twice on Good; prominent style means he can slot directly behind Sir Allen and strike before hold-up horses organise — the last run was a disappointing dash-marked effort, but the earlier form line (1-1-3) on similar ground is solid.
runners_data.comment: A winner three starts back, and four starts back, he was third two starts back before a sixth last time out, but already has today's trip and going under his belt. Fourth on our figures, the question is whether he rediscovers that earlier scoring form.

runners_data.name: Dontgowithjoe
runners_data.note: 328-day layoff is a major flag for a five-year-old returning cold; two wins came on Good ground over similar trips so the conditions suit in theory, but a hold-up style and such a long absence mean he needs everything to fall right and hold-up types are crowded in this field.
runners_data.comment: Two wins in his last four starts catch the eye, but a 328-day absence and a yard managing just one winner from 21 in the last fortnight are hard to ignore. He does have today's trip and going covered, but ranks ninth of ten on our figures.

runners_data.name: Ballyearl
runners_data.note: Prominent style (headgear: tongue-tie) and Henry De Bromhead stable 5/30 in T14; won on Good 17f previously but last three runs disappoint, and the 21-day turnaround after a pulled-up run requires scrutiny — should be ridden to track the pace but form profile is fragile.
runners_data.comment: A winner four starts back but well below that since, with a sixth, an unplaced run, and a pulled-up effort last time out. He has today's trip and going covered, and sits sixth on our figures off a 21-day break, with the recent stumble the main concern.

runners_data.name: Eye Of A Tiger
runners_data.note: JJ Slevin takes the ride on a hold-up type whose true closing style is squeezed into a congested midfield by the redistribution — his STYLE_FIT 0.92 tag reflects he is not in his natural race position, and a 43-day absence compounds the concern; best two runs came over 16f on Good so the trip is within range if traffic clears.
runners_data.comment: A third five starts back is the highlight in a run since undone by an unseat and finishes no better than fifth, including a ninth last time. Winless in her last five starts but with today's trip and going covered, our figures rate her well above her official mark.

runners_data.name: Eye Contact
runners_data.note: Flagged as fading in the finish and STYLE_FIT 0.90; a true hold-up horse shuffled into midfield by the crowded rear, Alan O'Sullivan (5) takes over after a 10-day turnaround — the recent form reads 0-0-4-6 and the course form on Good shows no wins from nine similar-going runs.
runners_data.comment: A sixth last time and a fourth before that follow two unplaced efforts further back, leaving him winless in his last four starts. Quick to return here just 10 days on, with today's trip and going covered, our figures still nudge him above his official mark.

runners_data.name: Free Flow
runners_data.note: 121-day absence for this hold-up type operating off a low OR of 100; Edward Power yard has 0/2 in T14, and the horse has finished outside the top six in seven of its last eight hurdle starts on Good — the redistribution means it is shown in midfield but in reality will be trying to close from the rear into a compressed field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts with nothing better than a seventh among mostly unplaced efforts, and he returns here from a 121-day absence. He does have today's trip and going covered, and our figures still nudge him a touch above his official mark.

runners_data.name: Space Warrior
runners_data.note: Thomas Mullins runner returning after 98 days, a genuine hold-up type pushed into midfield by the redistribution (STYLE_FIT 0.91); best recent run was a third on Good over 17f, but the form string 6-4-P-6-3 lacks consistency and the yard has 0/4 in T14 — needs a near-perfect run from an awkward starting position.
runners_data.comment: A third last time out is the pick of an otherwise mixed book of a pulled-up run and two sixths, and he's winless in his last five. Today's trip and going are covered, but a 98-day break and bottom spot on our figures make him hard to fancy.

races.paceDynamic: Sir Allen is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival disputing early, he is likely to bowl along at a sustainable gallop from flag to finish on Good ground at Ballinrobe. That controlled, uncontested tempo suits hold-up horses who can travel smoothly in behind and launch one clean run in the straight, rather than grinders who need a punishing pace to be set. Wolf Prince (10-year-old but in cracking form, two recent wins) and Fiveonefive (Mark Walsh booking notable) are the natural beneficiaries, with Spinola Bay the prominent type best placed to track Sir Allen without getting into a dogfight. The field contains far more hold-up types than can realistically settle at the rear — Eye Of A Tiger, Free Flow, Eye Contact and Space Warrior are all true closers pushed into a congested midfield by the redistribution, meaning their finishing kicks may be blunted by traffic and the lack of a searching pace to aim at; this race shape most strongly favours a single, well-timed hold-up runner who can find clear daylight in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Sir Allen dictates an uncontested, even gallop and hold-up horses land a clean run from the home turn.
scenarios.body: Sir Allen idles in front on Good ground, creating a compressed field where one well-positioned closer can sprint past; the lack of pressure means only a horse with a sharp turn of foot can peel out and quicken.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Outstays
scenarios.trigger: If Spinola Bay tracks Sir Allen throughout and kicks decisively from two out before hold-up horses can organise.
scenarios.body: Jack Kennedy slots Spinola Bay into second, the pair stride clear entering the straight, and hold-up types face too much ground to make up on a flat Good surface; Spinola Bay's two previous wins on Good give him a solid course-going profile.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Free Gallop
scenarios.trigger: If Sir Allen sets a stronger-than-expected gallop and ties up late, leaving the race wide open for hold-up horses to swoop.
scenarios.body: Any increase in early tempo would hollow Sir Allen out over this 2m1½f trip, and a genuine late rush could benefit a horse that has been tracking at the back of midfield; however, the redistribution means several supposed closers are not truly settled at the rear, diluting the likelihood of a clean late sweep.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Grinder Grinds Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just sufficient to string the field out and a consistent, grinding hold-up type wears down the leaders between the last two flights.
scenarios.body: A mid-tempo race that neither collapses nor accelerates suits a horse with relentless staying power rather than a sprint finish; the compressed midfield reduces this scenario's likelihood because genuine closers are not in their natural position and true prominent types have already taken the front.

watchPoints.text: Sir Allen's gallop sets the entire race — watch whether Sam Coen (5) allows him to coast or tries to inject pace from the front, as any acceleration will dramatically reduce the time hold-up horses have to close.

Dontgowithjoe returns from 328 days off; if he shows rustiness jumping or fails to travel, the hold-up brigade loses one of its more credentialled members and the scenario matrix shifts further toward Spinola Bay.

The redistributed closers — Eye Of A Tiger, Free Flow, Eye Contact and Space Warrior — will all be competing for the same ground in midfield; watch for a wall of horses entering the straight that blocks the one legitimate late finisher in the field.

Jack Kennedy on Spinola Bay is the most significant jockey deployment in this field — if he elects to sit closer to Sir Allen than expected rather than tracking at a distance, it signals stable confidence and a front-two breakaway scenario is live.

Wolf Prince's 9-day turnaround is short but the trainer has a live T14 strike rate (1/2); watch for whether the yard runs him fresh or if there is any sign of race-day market support that confirms he has trained on from his last win.

races.name: Sweeney Oil Handicap Hurdle (Div I)

runners_data.name: Tannery Park
runners_data.note: Hold-up galloper for Barry Connell, ridden by Mark Walsh; 420 days off is the obvious concern, but this trip and Good ground suit his profile — the fade-in-finish flag is worth noting in a 19-runner slog.|
runners_data.comment: Won last time out after modest efforts either side of an unplaced run, but a 420-day absence since is the concern. Has raced over today's trip and going before, and rates fourth of 19 on our figures.

runners_data.name: Bearami Creek
runners_data.note: Peter Fahey hold-up type returning after 72 days; decent recent form on Good ground, placed twice at this sort of trip, though the sim-going record of 12/13 runs without a win is telling.|
runners_data.comment: Unplaced last time out, with a pulled-up effort before that. A fifth four starts back and a fourth five starts back hinted at more, but she is yet to win in her last five; she has raced over today's going before and sits second of 19 on our figures.

runners_data.name: Madame Masque
runners_data.note: De Bromhead mare who has fallen away badly in her last three — all on Heavy, so the step back to Good is a clear positive — but 205 days off and a consistent fade-in-finish flag make this a wait-and-see.|
runners_data.comment: Won four starts back but has found only unplaced form in three runs since, and a 205-day absence adds to the concern. That was still enough for a big form step, and she rates third of 19 on our figures.

runners_data.name: It's Time Again
runners_data.note: Prominent-style veteran of ten who handles Good ground and this trip well; the hurdle fall on recent form is a concern, but Liam McKenna claims 3lb and the horse's five Good-ground outings show he knows how to compete at this distance.|
runners_data.comment: Fell last time out and pulled up two starts back — a discouraging recent sequence — though she has raced over today's trip and going before. Winless in her last four, she rates sixth of 19 on our figures.

runners_data.name: Run For The Border
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed pace-setter; Michael Kenneally (5lb claimer) rides, and on Good ground over 2m6f with no one to push him, an uncontested lead is within reach — STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 signals he is technically slightly outside his most natural profile, temper expectations accordingly.|
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and a winner four starts back, sandwiched between two moderate efforts. Has raced over today's going before, and sits ninth of 19 on our figures — respectable without standing out.

runners_data.name: Vroomvroomboo
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for James Fahey with a 7lb claimer aboard; sim-going record of 14/15 runs at Good without a win is damaging and the distance is towards the outer edge of what he has managed.|
runners_data.comment: Modest recent form — eighth last time out and no better than fifth twice since — but she sits well above her official mark on our figures at 92, fifth of 19. Has raced over today's trip and going before, without a win in her last five.

runners_data.name: Coppola
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott runner who has placed three times in four recent Good-ground runs over 24f — the fade-in-finish flag is notable — but consistent placed efforts suggest he stays well and travels; hold-up style means traffic in a 19-runner field is the chief danger.|
runners_data.comment: Three straight seconds form a platform, but two pulled-up efforts since, including last time out, are hard to ignore. Yet to win in her last five, sitting 14th of 19 on our figures, though she has raced over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Ranger Billy
runners_data.note: Prominent horse with J J Slevin up; two wins and three places from 15 Good-ground runs show reliability, and this 2m6f trip over hurdles is exactly his range — DNFs on recent form are a yellow flag.|
runners_data.comment: Three pulled-up efforts in his last four starts make for grim reading, though he sits well above his official mark on our figures at 90, seventh of 19. Has raced over today's trip and going before, but needs to complete a race.

runners_data.name: Whatyouwant
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner who was last out just 11 days ago; two Good-ground wins from 15 runs and the 2m6f+ trip suits, with G B Noonan riding — a fresh enough horse who should be able to dictate a position.|
runners_data.comment: A win four starts back is the standout, with modest efforts either side since, including a fifth last time out. Quick to reappear just eleven days on, she's raced over today's trip and going before and sits at 85 on our figures, tenth of 19.

runners_data.name: Not So Serious
runners_data.note: Danny Mullins takes this 5-year-old for W J Lanigan; genuinely a hold-up/rear type pushed into the midfield section on the map due to overcrowding — STYLE_FIT 0.90 confirms it is not in its natural position, and form of 0-0PPP with the fade-in-finish flag is hard to overcome.|
runners_data.comment: Our figures rate him clear of this field at 103, top of 19, despite three pulled-up efforts and two unplaced finishes in his last five. Quick to return after just 11 days, he remains the one to beat, though completing his round is the obvious ask.

runners_data.name: Tantrum Boy
runners_data.note: Six-year-old for Brian McMahon with Phillip Enright; similarly redistributed from its true hold-up position — its natural finish-late style is compromised in this shape, and a sim-going record of 3 from 5 placed runs is modest at best.|
runners_data.comment: A poor recent sequence, including three unplaced runs and an eighth last time out, leaves little to like, and he's rated down at 67 on our figures, 17th of 19 — hard to fancy without firm evidence of improvement.

runners_data.name: Coole Vision
runners_data.note: Peter Smithers (7lb) aboard this nine-year-old for Norman Lee; genuinely a hold-up horse that has been pushed into midfield on the map — only one sim-going run in Good conditions from nine starts flags a real going concern, and the form string is unremarkable.|
runners_data.comment: A stop-start record — two pulled-up efforts, an unplaced run and a fourth — leaves him winless in his last four. Has raced over today's going before, and sits 13th of 19 on our figures, with little consistency to build a case on.

runners_data.name: Will It Be You
runners_data.note: Brian Hayes rides for Liam Cusack; natural hold-up type squeezed into midfield representation — the fade-in-finish flag and a 15-day turnaround are noted, and the best Going sim-form run was a placed 8th, which is not compelling.|
runners_data.comment: A ninth last time out continues a run of little form, following a pulled-up effort and an unplaced run before that. He has raced over today's trip and going before, though sits 12th of 19 on our figures, winless in his last four.

runners_data.name: Lost Features
runners_data.note: Philip Donovan on this six-year-old for Darren Collins, who runs just nine days after its last start; redistributed from hold-up position, and the recent form of P9-98P with fade-in-finish flag does not suggest a horse about to turn the corner.|
runners_data.comment: Pulled up twice in her last five starts, with a pair of ninths and an eighth in between offering little to cling to. Back in action just nine days after her latest run, she remains unexposed and open to improvement, though the evidence so far is thin.

runners_data.name: John Dixen
runners_data.note: Simon Torrens rides this four-year-old for P J Rothwell; only one Good-ground run from five and all recent hurdle form reads poorly — pushed into midfield from its natural hold-up position, the age and form combination are both negatives.|
runners_data.comment: A sixth last time out is the highlight of a largely unplaced sequence that also includes a pulled-up effort, and he's winless in his last five. Has run over today's distance before, but sits down at 70 on our figures, 16th of 19 — a big task from here.

runners_data.name: Sineads Fancy
runners_data.note: Prominent-style mare with Cian Quirke up for S Ryan; sim-going record of 12/15 on Good without a win is worrying, but three placed finishes and one win over a similar trip in better conditions show she stays well.|
runners_data.comment: A third four starts back is the standout, but form has since tailed off to seventh and ninth in her last two. Has raced over today's trip and going before, and she's up at 82 on our figures, 15th of 19, though winless throughout her last five.

runners_data.name: Light Her Up
runners_data.note: Reserve 1 ride for Hugh Paul Finegan; 220 days off the track is a major concern — a natural hold-up type redistributed into midfield on the map, and the sim-going record of 6 from 8 placed on Good ground shows ability but nothing definitive.|
runners_data.comment: A fourth three starts back sits between two sixths, with an unplaced effort last time out rounding off a moderate sequence. A 220-day absence since is the biggest concern, though she has raced over today's going before and sits 11th of 19 on our figures.

runners_data.name: My Good Pal
runners_data.note: Reserve 2 ride for Gavin Cromwell; prominent-to-hold-up profile with a genuine placed effort over 24f on Good ground recently — the unseat on latest run (U in form) needs context but Cromwell's horses are reliable, and this trip is right in range.|
runners_data.comment: A second three starts back is the highlight, backed by a fifth four starts back, but he has since been unseated and finished eighth last time out. Yet to win in his last five, he has raced over today's trip and going before and sits eighth of 19 on our figures.

runners_data.name: Ballinaboola Hanna
runners_data.note: Reserve 3 ride for R Donohoe; five-year-old with only one sim-going run from six on Good, and 98 days off — hold-up style with no strong angles to project, though the yard runs horses fresh and the trip has not been fully tested.|
runners_data.comment: A modest sequence of ninth, sixth, a fall, fifth and seventh leaves little to shout about, and she remains without a win in her last five. Back after a 98-day break, she's unexposed enough that the form so far shouldn't be taken as the final word.

races.paceDynamic: Run For The Border is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field and is likely to bowl along at a sustainable, uncontested gallop on Good ground over 2m6f — a trip that will test stamina without a genuine pace duel to expose it early. The redistribution note is important here: Light Her Up, Tantrum Boy, Not So Serious, Coole Vision and several others are natural hold-up or prominent types who will struggle to find their preferred position in such a large, competitive field, meaning the midfield is likely to be densely packed and tactically messy. With one pace-setter dictating an honest but not breakneck tempo, the race is set up to reward horses who travel prominently just behind the leader and have the stamina to grind on from the second-last — prominent racers and hold-up types with a relentless galloping style rather than a sharp turn of foot are favoured. In a race this size, those who can hold a clean position in the first half without burning energy in traffic will have a meaningful edge over the compressed midfield.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Run For The Border sets a steady pace and horses who can sit just behind in the first three or four hold position throughout, the race is run at a rhythm that suits gallopers who travel well.
scenarios.body: Run For The Border dictates from the front while It's Time Again, Whatyouwant and Ranger Billy track in the first five, all in their natural roles; the steady pace means they do not need to produce a quick turn of foot, just outstay rivals late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo stays sufficiently steady that Run For The Border is never seriously pressured and simply gallops rivals into submission on this stamina-testing 2m6f trip.
scenarios.body: Run For The Border, travelling comfortably through a large, untidy field, hits the home straight with enough in reserve to hold on; Good ground and a single honest gallop rewards a front-runner that is fit and confident.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pick Up Pieces
scenarios.trigger: If the first circuit is more contested than expected and the pace quickens sufficiently to string out the field, leaving prominent horses flat from the last.
scenarios.body: Horses who sit off the pace in the early stages and produce a sustained gallop from the second-last can pick through tired rivals; Tannery Park, Bearami Creek and My Good Pal are the best-credentialled to benefit, though their ability to find a clean run through a big field is a material risk.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Traffic Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the large, compacted field causes interference, checks and positional battles in the back straight, producing an uneven pace and a lottery finish.
scenarios.body: With so many redistributed hold-up types forced into midfield and a field of 19, interference incidents are a genuine risk; any horse that avoids trouble and gets a clean run from mid-division could benefit, but this is the least predictable shape.

watchPoints.text: Run For The Border — watch whether Michael Kenneally allows the horse to stride on unchallenged from the gate; if he gets a soft lead, the price could dramatically compress as the field fails to close the gap over this stamina trip.

The compressed midfield cluster — with seven or more redistributed hold-up types forced into the body of the field, monitor early for scrimmaging and checked horses between the first and fourth hurdle; a single incident here could eliminate multiple fancied runners.

Tannery Park — Mark Walsh takes a 420-day absentee into a 19-runner handicap; watch the market closely for any significant support, which would signal stable confidence in a horse whose last win was over 22f on Good.

Coppola — three consecutive placed efforts on Good ground in this trip range makes him a quiet each-way danger if Gordon Elliott has this horse fit enough, despite the fade-in-finish flag; watch how sharply he travels into the back straight second time.

My Good Pal — Cromwell's prominent-style horse with a reserve jockey is worth monitoring; if a named jockey is announced before the off, upgrade the interest level, as Cromwell rarely pitches this type of horse into a big handicap without a plan.

races.name: Sweeney Oil Handicap Hurdle (Div II)

runners_data.name: Pourquoi Poi

runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and a third three starts back too, sandwiched around being brought down - still without a win in the last five starts. Race-fit after nine days and has run over today's going; carries 166 lb, rated 93 and ninth of 19.

runners_data.name: Smackwater Jack
runners_data.note: Aged 12 but showed a course win over 24f on Good recently; T14 return of 1/2 is a positive signal from Mrs Foster's yard, and his prominent style suits this controlled pace — one of the most interesting each-way profiles in the race.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out; a win two starts back is the pick of the form, with a ninth, an unplaced effort and a seventh further back in the book. Has run over today's trip and going before, carrying 165 lb fresh from a 36-day break; rated 93 and eighth of 19.

runners_data.name: Fool Me Once
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse trained by Cromwell who hasn't run in 74 days; sim-going figures are modest (0W3P on Good), and without a strong pace to close into, his chances of arriving late enough look slim.
runners_data.comment: Recent starts read modestly - unplaced in three of the last five, either side of a pulled-up run and a fifth - yet still holds the standout figure on our book at 103. Main risk: 74 days off and a yard managing just 2 from 41 (5%) in the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: Joshua Chamberlain
runners_data.note: Prominent type with a win over 21f on Soft; Good-ground form reads 0W1P from 11 runs, which is the concern, but he stays this trip and Ricky Doyle gives him a clear positional chance from the early stages.
runners_data.comment: Unplaced last time out, but a win three starts back - flanked by a pair of fifths - is the form to focus on. Has run over today's trip and going before and returns from 69 days off carrying 164 lb; rated 98 and fourth of 19.

runners_data.name: Rushford
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with a 'fades in finish' flag and all recent form at much shorter trips (8-12f) — the step up to 2m6f looks a significant ask, and the form profile suggests this trip and ground combination is a tough ask.
runners_data.comment: Pulled up last time out and again three starts back, either side of a fifth, with a ninth and sixth further back, still without a win in the last five. Fresh off just 12 days' rest and rated well above its 90 mark at 98, third of 19.

runners_data.name: She'll Be Kept
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse who has placed over 22f on Good; Phillip Enright rides and the mare showed a 3rd over this sort of trip only recently — the stamina is there if the race develops into a test, though the controlled pace limits her scenario.
runners_data.comment: A second three starts back is the standout in a mixed book that also shows a sixth, an unplaced effort, a fall and an unseated exit. Fresh off just 19 days, with experience over today's trip and going, and rated 103 - the case for this being the pick here.

runners_data.name: Whiskey Serenade
runners_data.note: Hold-up profile with a second on Good over 20f in recent form; Eoghan Finegan (5) is the lightest senior-ish claim in the race, and 17 days since last run is a normal prep — needs the race to develop into a proper stamina test to be competitive.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out but the four starts before that read 6th, unplaced, 7th and 9th - a mixed book that leaves plenty to prove. Fresh off 17 days, with experience over today's trip and going, but only an 88 rating and eleventh of 19 here.

runners_data.name: Yolanda's Star
runners_data.note: Unknown style (listed as U) with only three career runs, all on Good; 'fades in finish' flag is a concern over 2m6f, and the limited sample size makes it very hard to assess — Joshua Halford is a 7lb claimer adding further uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out having finished eighth and unplaced in the two starts before that - a sparse book of just three starts, still without a win in that spell. Fresh off a 36-day break, with experience over today's trip and going, rated 93 and tenth of 19.

runners_data.name: Stumblin In
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose sim-going figures over similar trips on Good are among the weaker in the field (1W2P from 14 runs on Good but positional finishes are low); O'Sullivan's 5lb claim helps the weight but the profile is of a modest handicapper needing a lot to go right.
runners_data.comment: A largely unplaced book - three such efforts either side of a sixth and a seventh - leaves little to shout about, still without a win in the last five starts. Fresh off 19 days, with experience over today's trip and going, rated 88 and twelfth of 19.

runners_data.name: Strong Contender
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse in reality — J J Slevin is a strong booking and the 3/26f on Good in his history is the one distance-relevant data point of interest, but REDISTRIBUTED and STYLE_FIT flags confirm he won't get his natural trailing position here, which blunts his chance materially.
runners_data.comment: A third five starts back is the high point of a book otherwise filled with a seventh, two unplaced efforts and a fall, and still without a win. Fresh off a 36-day break with experience over today's going, but rated only 75 and sixteenth of 19.

runners_data.name: Granlahan
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with consistent placed form (three 3rds on Good in recent months); Darragh O'Keeffe is one of the stronger rides in the race and the trainer's T14 of 2/28 shows active form — unexposed angle at this trip is the appeal.
runners_data.comment: Three thirds in the last five starts, broken up by one unseated exit, with an eighth also in the mix - still without a win. Race-fit after just 11 days with experience over today's going, rated 86 and thirteenth of 19.

runners_data.name: Jolly Potter
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a 'fades in finish' flag and only three recent runs, none on Good ground; mapped to midfield due to redistribution but his true trailing style and limited form make this look a tough task — Conor Smithers (7) is an inexperienced claimer aboard.
runners_data.comment: Yet to find the frame in its last four starts - two unplaced efforts followed by an eighth and a seventh - but lightly raced enough to leave room for improvement. Returns from 67 days off carrying 149 lb, an 80 official rating to work with.

runners_data.name: Mollys Dolly
runners_data.note: Natural closer whose recent form reads PP-560, none of which are encouraging; mapped to midfield due to the depth of hold-up types in this field but her actual position in running is likely to be further back, making the task even harder over 2m6f on Good.
runners_data.comment: A modest book showing an unplaced run, a sixth and a fifth in its last three starts, with two pulled-up efforts further back - still without a win in the last five. Fresh off 19 days with experience over today's going, rated 80 and fifteenth of 19.

runners_data.name: La Tene
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old veteran with a form string of P39F-P and 61 days since last run; his true hold-up style sees him shuffled to midfield on the map, but Good-ground sim data of 4/10 is limited and the pattern of pullovers and mid-race blunders does not inspire confidence.
runners_data.comment: Two pulled-up efforts and a fall dominate a difficult book that also shows a ninth and a third, still without a win in the last five starts. Returns from 61 days off carrying 141 lb, rated 74 and seventeenth of 19.

runners_data.name: Lady Aquarelle
runners_data.note: 'Fades in finish' flag combined with a REDISTRIBUTED tag makes this a difficult combination to work with; Thomas Cooper's filly has struggled on Good (2/6 sim-going) and the OR of 72 is the lowest competitive weight in the field — a tough assignment.
runners_data.comment: A consistently modest book - a pulled-up run, a seventh, eighth, ninth and an unplaced effort - leaves little in its favour, still without a win in the last five starts. Fresh off 19 days with experience over today's trip and going, rated 66 and eighteenth of 19.

runners_data.name: Toor Moon
runners_data.note: 9-year-old prominent type with four recent placed efforts but all on Good and Soft at trips between 22-24f — the distance is well within range, but a string of 0s in recent form and a sim-going record of 0W4P suggests he's been running well without winning for some time.
runners_data.comment: An unseated exit and two unplaced efforts dominate the book, though a third five starts back hints at more. Fresh off 38 days with experience over today's trip and going, rated 11 lb above its 72 mark at 83, fourteenth of 19.

runners_data.name: Leis Fein
runners_data.note: 242 days off the track is a major flag; the 11-year-old has form on Good over 18f but the absence alone warrants significant caution, and the trainer (V T O'Brien, T14: 0/1) shows no recent winning form to suggest this is a prep comeback in good order.
runners_data.comment: Pulled up last time out and again three starts back, either side of a sixth, with a fourth four starts back - still without a win in the last four starts. A lengthy 242-day absence is the concern, but rated 15 lb above its 82 mark at 97, fifth of 19.

runners_data.name: John Storey
runners_data.note: Prominent type but the form string of 6P4PP reads poorly and the horse has no jockey listed in the data — the trip and Good ground are familiar enough, but sim-going record of 0W0P and a 100-day absence makes this look like a race-fit exercise.
runners_data.comment: Three pulled-up efforts dominate a difficult book that also shows a fourth and a sixth, still without a win in the last five starts. Returns from 100 days off with experience over today's trip and going, carrying 159 lb; rated 94 and seventh of 19.

runners_data.name: Ladiam
runners_data.note: The standout profile for the dominant scenario — nine runs on Good, sim-going record of 1W6P, distances all clustered around 20-22f, trained by Norman Lee who also runs Strong Contender, and a last run of 56 days is a conventional enough prep; a prominent galloper whose consistency on Good ground makes him the biggest danger to Pourquoi Poi.
runners_data.comment: A third four starts back and a second five starts back mark the high points of a book since cooled to two fifths and a seventh, without a win in the last five. Fresh off 56 days with experience over today's trip and going; rated 96, sixth of 19.

races.paceDynamic: Pourquoi Poi is the one confirmed front-runner in this 19-runner field and, crucially, faces no obvious challenger for the lead — on Good ground over 2m6f at Ballinrobe, that means a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front with Jack Kennedy able to dictate terms entirely on his own terms. Behind him, Smackwater Jack, Joshua Chamberlain, Granlahan, Ladiam, and Toor Moon are all natural prominent types who will press forward into the first two or three places, creating a compact front pack but not a truly contested early pace. The race will be run at an honest but measured tempo, stretching out over this 2m6f trip with the shape unlikely to dramatically accelerate until after the final turn, favouring horses who can travel prominently or in the first half of the field and sustain their effort rather than those who need a truly fast pace to bring them into the race. The dominant tactical verdict here is clear: prominent-to-midfield runners with strong stamina at this trip on Good ground are best served — genuine hold-up horses are disadvantaged because the pace is unlikely to be pressured enough to bring them from the rear in time. This field carries more hold-up types than the map can honestly place at the rear — Strong Contender, Jolly Potter, Mollys Dolly, La Tene, and Lady Aquarelle are all true closers redistributed to midfield, and of those, Jolly Potter and La Tene are least likely to secure any meaningful forward position given their form profiles.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pourquoi Poi Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Pourquoi Poi is allowed to coast from the front unchallenged and the pace remains measured enough that no hold-up horse can close the gap.
scenarios.body: Kennedy dictates a controlled gallop, the front pack settles into a rhythm, and Pourquoi Poi's stamina over this 2m6f trip on Good ground sees him hold on as rivals fail to reel him in from mid-race. Prominent horses who travel smoothly into the race and have course-proven stamina — Ladiam and Smackwater Jack — are the most dangerous, having the profile to sit within striking range and pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Collar Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Ladiam or Smackwater Jack track Pourquoi Poi comfortably and have enough in reserve to overhaul him from the second-last flight.
scenarios.body: Ladiam's excellent recent Good-ground form at this distance and Smackwater Jack's course experience make them natural threats to a front-runner who is, strictly, operating slightly out of profile based on STYLE_FIT data. The stamina-loaded profiles of both prominent types suit a race run at a controlled tempo where the final 2f becomes the deciding factor.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Stayer Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected — pushed by Smackwater Jack or Joshua Chamberlain — and a genuine stamina test unfolds that brings a staying hold-up type into the mix.
scenarios.body: She'll Be Kept or Whiskey Serenade, both of whom have shown ability to close on Good ground at around this trip, could benefit if the early leaders burn each other off and the closing stages become a stamina grind. However, this scenario is tempered by the number of redistributed closers in the field who are unlikely to be in their true position, reducing the chance that the right horse is actually settled far enough back to deliver a late run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Granlahan Youth Shocks Field
scenarios.trigger: If Granlahan's younger legs and consistent placed form allow him to travel prominently and find extra where older rivals tire late.
scenarios.body: At four years old with a solid string of placed efforts on Good ground, Granlahan represents the unexposed angle in this competitive handicap if Darragh O'Keeffe can secure a handy position and produce him with a run from the second-last. This remains a low-probability outcome given the strength of the likely front group and the horse's current OR, but the age profile and trainer's recent form make him a live outside threat.

watchPoints.text: Pourquoi Poi — if Jack Kennedy is allowed to bowl along uncontested in the early stages with no rival willing to press him, the entire field is chasing a horse who controls his own fractions over 2m6f on Good ground.

Ladiam — his sim-going record (1W6P from 13 runs on Good) and prominent style make him the most credible threat to the leader; watch where he settles in the first mile, as a position just off Pourquoi Poi could be decisive late.

Smackwater Jack — the 12-year-old's T14 booking (1/2) from Mrs Foster's yard suggests he's fit and primed; age is against him but a prominent pitch in a controlled-pace race over a trip he's handled before makes him worth monitoring from the outset.

Strong Contender and Jolly Potter — both are genuine closers mapped forward on the diagram due to redistribution; if either ends up further back than their map position suggests, the slow pace may leave them with too much to do from the final turn.

Granlahan — four-year-old with Darragh O'Keeffe in the saddle is the one runner with a youth profile in this field; watch for him to be produced with a run from the second-last, as his unexposed stamina profile at 2m6f is the most interesting unknown in the race.

runners_data.name: Ballybollen
runners_data.comment: Ballybollen is unraced and makes his debut here, with nothing on the book yet to judge him by. He carries 168 lb and is a complete form-book blank, unexposed and unproven on his first start.

runners_data.name: Colga Boys
runners_data.comment: Colga Boys is unraced and untested on his debut, with no working form yet to go on. He carries 168 lb and remains a blank slate, entirely open to what he shows on debut.

runners_data.name: Ealu Tapa
runners_data.comment: Ealu Tapa was 9th on his only start to date, 45 days ago, and is yet to win in that solitary run. Still finding his feet at an early stage, he carries 168 lb here.

runners_data.name: Josh's Jury
runners_data.comment: Josh's Jury was 8th on his only start, a long way back now at 304 days ago, and remains without a win. Fresh off a lengthy absence, he carries 168 lb and has plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: Long Story
runners_data.comment: Long Story has been 7th in both his starts to date, most recently 36 days ago, without troubling the judge for a win either time. Lightly raced and yet to click, he carries 168 lb.

runners_data.name: Merci Vieil Ami
runners_data.comment: Merci Vieil Ami has failed to complete in both his starts to date, pulled up last time out 87 days ago having unseated on the run before that. Still winless as a result, he carries 168 lb and remains a work in progress.

runners_data.name: Millers Point
runners_data.comment: Millers Point has failed to complete on both his starts to date, pulled up each time, and hasn't been seen since 479 days ago. A long time off the track and still winless, he carries 168 lb on his return.

runners_data.name: Moundofthehostages
runners_data.comment: Moundofthehostages has been unplaced in both his starts to date, most recently 37 days ago, and remains without a win. Still finding his level on this scant evidence, he carries 168 lb here.

runners_data.name: Saviour Blu
runners_data.comment: Saviour Blu was unseated last time out, 15 days ago, having finished unplaced on the run before that, and remains without a win in his two starts to date. Quick to reappear, he carries 168 lb.

runners_data.name: Srah
runners_data.comment: Srah is unraced and makes his debut here, with no working form to go on. He carries 168 lb and is very much one to watch with an open mind rather than assess on evidence.

runners_data.name: Tommy's Ticket
runners_data.comment: Tommy's Ticket was 6th on his only start, 36 days ago, and is yet to win in that solitary outing. He wears a hood here and carries 168 lb, with more expected as he gains experience.

runners_data.name: Hometomayo
runners_data.comment: Hometomayo was a 4th last time out, 65 days ago, having pulled up in each of her previous three starts. She remains without a win in that sequence and carries 161 lb here.

runners_data.name: Pamelaisbrass
runners_data.comment: Pamelaisbrass was unplaced last time out, 17 days ago, having finished 6th on the run before that, and is yet to win in two starts. She carries 161 lb on a quick reappearance.
